questions.prompt: Match each component to what it does.

pairs.right: Lights up, but only one way round

questions.explain: Each part of a circuit has a job.

options: it touches one terminal of the cell
it is part of a complete, closed loop with the cell
questions.explain: Current needs an unbroken path from one terminal, through the bulb, back to the other terminal.

questions.prompt: In the Circuit Builder, a second cell was added (both facing the same way). The bulb…
questions.explain: Two cells push more current, making the bulb brighter.

questions.prompt: Two cells are placed facing OPPOSITE ways in a circuit. What happens?
options: The bulb is twice as bright
Their pushes cancel and the bulb doesn't light
questions.explain: Cells must be joined + to − so their pushes add.

questions.prompt: Two bulbs are in series. One is unscrewed. What happens to the other?
questions.explain: A series circuit has only one path; a gap anywhere stops the current.

questions.prompt: Why are the lights and fans in your home connected in parallel, not in series?
options: Each appliance gets the full voltage and can be switched on and off independently
questions.explain: In parallel, each branch works on its own.

questions.prompt: Plan an experiment to test whether the number of cells affects the brightness of a bulb. How could you measure brightness fairly?
questions.modelAnswer: Independent variable: the number of cells in series (1, 2, 3). Dependent variable: brightness, measured with a light-meter app on a phone held at the same distance from the bulb in a dark room (or by comparing with a reference bulb). Control variables: the same bulb, the same wires, the same phone position, and new cells of the same type. Take readings quickly so the bulb doesn't overheat, and repeat each reading.
rubric: A fair way to measure brightness
questions.explain: Criterion B: turning ‘brightness’ into a measurement.

questions.text: A cell has two terminals: positive (+) and ___. Two or more cells joined together make a ___.
questions.explain: The long line in the symbol is +, the short thick line is −.
